AITA for refusing to re-rack my weights at the gym? | I know it's proper gym ettiquete at most gyms to re-rack all your weights, that was the case at my last gym and I always re-racked my weights.

For the past 6 years I've been working out at my stations gym, I love it, has everything I need and usually I'm the only one working out. For the past 6 years I really only see the same 5-6 people working out at different times, everyone else comes in from time to time. I've repaired a lot of the equipment here from my own pocket, bring in gear like belts, chalk, rope, etc for everyone to use.

Well a few days ago I was squatting 225, after I was done with my sets, I took one 45 from each side off and left one 45 on both sides of the bar. I then went to do some deadlifts. In the middle of my set a woman(who I've never seen before) comes up to me and traps me on the shoulder. I put the weight down and take my headphones off. She asks me if I'm done with the squat rack, I said "yeah go ahead" and put my headphones back in. She motions again and says "well you need to put your weights back on the racks". I look at her with a confused look. She says that the weights can bend the bar (no they won't) and some people who work out there can't move 45 lbs by themselves (she wasn't talking about herself, I saw her benching 135). I told her if someone can't lift 45 lbs by themselves then they shouldn't be touching a barbell unattended( the bars are 45 lbs themselves), I then put my headphones back on and continued my workout ignoring her. She walked away mad and started to take pictures of the bar with the weights on and then pictures of me (idk what she was planning in doing with them and I didn't really care).
So my reasoning is this, there is not enough weigth trees for all the weights in the gym. In this gym it's customary to leave one 45 on each side of the bar, this includes the squat rack, all the bench presses, the deadlift area. Most people who workout here often are powerlifters, we just have this unwritten rule to leave the bar at 135, no more, no less. We rack the dumbbells and everything else but leave the bar at 135.
So AITA? I would have probably took the weights off if she didn't demand that I do so.
Sorry for format and any typos, on mobile.
agent_response:
UNETHICAL

The writer showed a lack of consideration for others by not re-racking his weights, and his justification that it's a customary practice at the gym doesn't excuse not making an effort to accommodate others. His response to the woman, including dismissing her concern and implying that those who can't lift 45 lbs shouldn't be working out, was also unhelpful and arrogant.

WIBTA if I distance myself from my niece? | I feel like I shouldn’t need to ask because of course I would be the asshole if I did this but I thought I would ask this sub for judgement just in case.

I have a three year old niece. When my sister went back to work after her daughter was born, the whole family kinda pitched in the help with childcare so they didn’t have to use a daycare. Her mother in law and our mother each looked after her for a few days a week. Eventually, with my extreme reluctance, I was rope in to help babysit maybe a total of seven day a month, sometimes more. Some of those day were super long, like eight hour days and I did this for about a year and a half. Somehow I become my niece’s favorite person during this time.

But I hate children. I’m childfree for a reason. And I’m not exactly big on my niece either but I suck it up because I’m adult enough to play nice with a small kid to help out my sister. But lately, it’s become harder and harder to do this. I’m not her mother so I defer to my sister in every case but it seems like the more I spend time with my niece the more my sister thinks I’m doing things wrong. Or saying the wrong things. I have to police all my actions and my words just in case my niece takes it the wrong way or it doesn’t align with her parents’ parenting plans and I am feeling judged for not knowing better.

Like yesterday we went to the park together. I was with my niece on the jungle gym and we were climbing it together. I got to a point where I wasn’t comfortable going any higher and I said “I’m going to go down because it’s scary” and immediately my niece didn’t want to go up any higher because she heard that and started parroting it. And now my sister is mad because I traumatized her daughter and peer pressured her daughter into limiting her possibilities because the person her daughter looked up to thought it was too scary. Okay, I’ll refrain from commenting about things being scary from now on if it’s damaging my niece so badly.

Things like this seem to be happening more and more but I’m starting to wondering if it’s really worth it. She’s not my kid, I don’t actually have a duty to be around her if anything I do or say is bad. I don’t even like kids and the way my niece is so fixated on me drives me a bit insane but I can suck it up because she’s a kid and I can eventually go home. But lately, I’m starting to wonder why I’m doing this in the first place if it just makes me miserable. So WIBTA if I pulled away?
agent_response:
ETHICAL

The writer has been going above and beyond to help with childcare, and has been shouldering the responsibility with a good attitude, despite not enjoying it. The constant criticism and judgment from their sister makes it clear that their efforts are not appreciated, and it's reasonable for them to consider distancing themselves to prioritize their own well-being. They have a right to set boundaries and not continue to subject themselves to a situation that makes them miserable.

AITA for putting restrictions on spousal friendships? | My spouse went on a solo vacation with a mutual friend of the opposite gender. I strongly argued against the trip, but I couldn't persuade my spouse it was a bad idea, so I reluctantly gave my "permission". In general my spouse has difficulty making and keeping friends, so I was trying to be supportive. During the trip they talked about many deep emotional topics, and my spouse found this connection to be very beneficial. They also drank heavily the entire trip and fell asleep together in a hammock at one point, but nothing happened beyond that (I am told). I feel very uncomfortable with how this has played out, especially because my spouse tends to be very flirtatious while drunk. I have asked my spouse to cut off the friendship, but my spouse feels this is a lot for me to ask because they have so few friends. Am I in the wrong here?
agent_response:
UNETHICAL

The writer is exhibiting possessive and controlling behavior by asking their spouse to cut off a friendship that doesn't involve actual infidelity. The spouse's actions on the trip, while potentially unwise, didn't cross any boundaries, and the writer's discomfort stems from their own insecurities rather than any objective issue with the friendship. Demanding that the spouse end the friendship due to the writer's own feelings is unreasonable and an overreach.

AITA for not offering friends my leftovers? | My boyfriend, two of his friends, and I were out at a diner. We all ordered (intending to pay separately, as usual) and I ultimately wasn't that hungry so halfway through I asked my boyfriend if he wanted to finish my plate. This is pretty common and the two friends would've almost certainly seen me do this before. He agreed so I pushed my plate over to him.

One of the friends said "well, *I'd* like some too" in a pissed off tone and started helping herself to my leftovers. The other friend said "yeah, me too" and took a piece of food from my plate as well. My boyfriend didn't say anything so neither did I, but the tone struck me as somewhat rude.

Was I the asshole for not offering them any to begin with? I felt like since it was my food, I would get to choose who ate it. As far as I can recall we never shared food while eating out.
agent_response:
ETHICAL

The writer had the right to control their own food and decide who they wanted to share it with, especially since they were paying for it themselves. The friends' expectation that they would be offered food and their tone when the writer didn't offer it were unwarranted and rude. The writer didn't owe them an explanation or an offer, and their decision to let their boyfriend have the leftovers was reasonable.
